The Guardian, 17 Nov 2026 06:37 GMT

Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join the next round of demonstrations ahead of the US president’s arrival in Manila for the Asean summit

Asean and Apec summits – live updates

Prefer the Guardian on GoogleHundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as authorities braced for more protests ahead of the US president’s arrival in the city for a leaders’ summit.

Organisers claim as many as 10,000 people will join protests against Trump in the Philippine capital on Tuesday, when he will attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds are expected to try to walk to the summit site.

Authorities have arrested nearly 300 people in widespread protests in held in the days leading up to the summit, with large parts of the capital closed off and tight security in place.

Read moreSome burned effigies of Trump and faced off with police officers armed with batons and shields. Slogans on placards called the American leader the world’s “number one terrorist” in protests held on Monday.

Demonstrators angry at the cost-of-living and energy shock caused by the Iran war, and the new US-led Pax Silica initiative on AI and critical minerals, tried to reach the summit at the Philippine International Convention Center on Monday, but were blocked by police.

Pax Silica has sparked tensions in the Philippines over plans to build a tech hub outside Manila that critics say will affect water and energy supplies, and displace members of the Ayta Indigenous community.

Large sections of central Manila were closed to the public as part of the security cordon, and public holidays instituted for the Asean summit.

Trump will meet with the leaders of Australia, Japan and India on Tuesday night before heading to Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday. There he will attend the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit and hold trilateral talks with China’s president, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin of Russia.

The backlash against Trump follows the ouster of Nvidia boss Jensen Huang, and allegations members of the US administration, including the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, knew about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump’s delegation was expected to include businessman Elon Musk.

Protest leader Renato Reyes blamed the arrests in Manila on the heavy handed response of the government on the president, Ferdinand Marcos Jr., calling Monday the largest single day of police arrests since Marcos came to office in 2022.

“It is really crazy that the Philippine government is rolling out the red carpet for someone who has been so flatly rejected by the American people,” Reyes said.

“Trump started a war that devastated the global economy and pushed oil prices in the Philippines to historic highs. It has caused untold suffering on the Filipino people.

“So yes, Trump will have to pay for his crimes and he will have to be answerable, not just to the American people, but to the people of the world.”

View image in fullscreenIndigenous communities and other groups protest in Manila on Monday.  Photograph: Nathaniel Soriano/ZUMA Press Wire/ShutterstockThe Philippine national police said some officers were injured during confrontations with demonstrators opposed to the summit, including when objects were allegedly thrown at officers.

Pax Silica will include a technology hub planned at New Clark City in Tarlac, about 120km from Manila.

Intended to bolster western stocks of AI technology and reduce “excessive dependencies” on single source supply chains, including from China, Pax Silica will provide chips and critical minerals to 25 participating signatory governments.

Amnesty Philippines said demonstrations should not be forcibly or violently dispersed.

“Reports of arrests during the protests demand immediate scrutiny,” director Ritz Lee Santos III said.

“Authorities must explain the specific grounds for each arrest and any continued detention. Anyone detained solely for peacefully exercising their rights must be released immediately.”
